newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: OSCE leaders, Gonzalez confer on Serbia report.
newsitem.headline: OSCE leaders, Gonzalez confer on Serbia report.

text.p: Former Spanish prime minister Felipe Gonzalez on Friday met top officials of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) to discuss his findings on contested elections in Serbia.

Gonzalez visited Belgrade last weekend at the head of an OSCE team invited by Serbia's President Slobodan Milosevic to look into opposition claims that his government fraudulently annulled the results of local polls last month.

OSCE officials said it was not yet clear whether a formal statement on the outcome of Gonzalez's investigations would be issued after talks with current OSCE president Flavio Cotti of Switzerland and incoming president Niels Petersen of Denmark.
Gonzalez, who now heads the socialist opposition in the Spanish parliament, declined to give any hint of his conclusions as he went into the meeting at Geneva's Hotel Intercontinental.
"I am an optimist, but it is a very complicated situation," he told reporters.
But he set a news conference for 2 p.m. (1300GMT), and OSCE sources said he was likely to make his views known then.

Since the elections on November 17, in which Serbian opposition parties say they scored stunning victories in Belgrade and several other centres, the Serbian capital has been the scene of massive daily demonstrations.

The Serbian government, after clashes between opposition and Milosevic supporters on Tuesday, has banned marches that disrupt traffic, fuelling a chorus of international criticism of his administration.
